memory_update.text: COHR and LITE should remain reference anchors for the AI photonics/InP device node; they define the commercial qualification and capacity benchmark rather than the underfollowed alpha lane.

AXTI is the strongest underfollowed substrate-level candidate to track for InP/GaAs/Ge wafer exposure, but survival to later layers depends on verified InP revenue, AI/datacenter customer pull, backlog, capacity, and dilution/geopolitical risk.

ALMU belongs in speculative_shadow only: possible III-V-on-silicon alternative platform for photonics scaling, but requires proof of commercial AI/datacom qualification, customer identity, revenue conversion, and cash-runway safety.

Fabrinet is a relevant second-order optical manufacturing beneficiary and should be considered in a separate EMS/precision optical assembly node; it was not included in the four-candidate list because this pass prioritized component/material/device bottlenecks.

node: Photonic components: InP lasers, photodetectors, precision substrates, and compound-semiconductor platforms
summary: Expanded the AI optical-photonics component node with a two-lane universe. Reference anchors are Coherent and Lumentum because they directly manufacture AI datacenter optical components, InP-based lasers/devices, and transceiver-related platforms. The underfollowed lane centers on AXT as a compound-semiconductor substrate supplier and Fabrinet as the precision optical manufacturing layer behind OEM and hyperscaler optical programs. Aeluma remains a speculative shadow candidate because its III-V-on-silicon platform could become relevant if native InP capacity remains constrained, but public commercial qualification evidence is still thin.
